html:
Welcome to the official RaggieSoft Backstage companion archive for Katie & Nathaniel.

Because every chapter of Katie & Nathaniel is written strictly in Nathaniel Prairie's first-person point of view, the main novel only shows what Nate and Katie can directly see, hear, and deduce in the moment. Whenever you encounter a Backstage Bonus Feature button at the end of a chapter on books.raggiesoft.com, you can open these behind-the-scenes and alternate "What If?" dossiers directly inside the reader without breaking narrative immersion.

1. Mainline Behind-the-Scenes & In-Era "What If?" Dossiers (2001–2044)

  1. Oct 19, 2001 — The Sunward Tropics Security File & How Brenda Lost the 'Prairie' Surname
    What happened behind closed doors when Brenda's attorney walked into Arthur Vance's conference room off Independence Boulevard to watch the M/S Sunward Tropics Deck 4 security tape—and how Katie and Nate's request forced Brenda to sign the Va. Code § 20-121.4 stipulation surrendering the Prairie family name and reverting to Brenda Walsh.
  2. Dec 31, 2002 — Alternate 'What If' Dossier: Hanging Up on Smoker's Corner — What If Brittany Respected Uncle David's No-Company Rule on New Year's Eve 2002?
    What happens if seventeen-year-old Brittany Fletcher remembers Nate's bus-loop no-company promise while Uncle David is in Newport, Rhode Island, hangs up on Tyler's party call, deadbolts the front door, rings in 2003 over ginger ale and pizza with Katie and Nate, graduates in the fourth purple gown in June 2003 (preventing Tyler's January 6 locker lie and sparing Brittany 13 lost years in South Richmond), tours ten colleges with rising-junior Wesley, and films her 1991 Crestline Garrison 350 (L-1-2-3-R) lessons with living Uncle David.
  3. Jan 11, 2003 — Five Red X's on the Wall Calendar: Wesley's Perspective on the Morning He Thought He Lost Nate Forever
    Told strictly from fifteen-year-old non-verbal Wesley Sorenson's third-person limited point of view on Saturday morning, January 11, 2003 in Chesapeake—revealing the sheer terror of having zero phone, bus, or spoken bridge to his very first guy friend Nate when Heather broke up with him, why Wesley blew up in heartbroken protest, and why he rescued the oak-framed November 2001 Annie's Pretzels photo off the living-room shelf to guard beside his bed until Graduation Day.
  4. Jan–Jun 2003 — Workstation Three, Cousin Hannah's Green Parka, & How Graduation 2003 Saved Our Bond
    What happened inside Senior Homeroom 212 on January 6 before Heather slammed her locker door, five weeks of Heather sitting alone beside two empty wheelchair spaces in Mr. Callahan's Room 204 lab while Crimson Node's "Unhandled Exception" echoed clear as day inside Nate's head in the back corner, the February 11 cafeteria lunch where Kristen Bauer and the Varsity Girls' Soccer team publicly roasted Tyler out of his seat—driving him out to lonely Brittany Fletcher at Smoker's Corner—plus Stairway A vs. the middle-loop bus stalls and welcoming Heather back cautiously for Wesley's sake at the Virginia Beach Pavilion.
  5. Oct 16–20, 2004 — CBSA Secondary Inspection at 35 Park Street East & The U.S. Marshals File on Brandon Mercer
    Reconstructs what happened between nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate's 4:00 PM six-bus escape from the Williamsburg Transportation Center (meeting Heather and Wesley on Monticello Avenue in Downtown Norfolk) and Brandon Mercer's arrest by Deputy U.S. Marshals at a men's shelter on Cass Avenue in Detroit—including his ripped-up ticket on East Jefferson Avenue, the Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus farebox trap, his refusal of entry into Canada at 555 Goyeau Street and 35 Park Street East in Windsor, Ontario, and the CBP seizure of his two contraband hard drives on Randolph Street.
  6. Dec 24–27, 2004 — Dirty Old Tonomy Hill & Why Brandon's Tunnel-Bus Scheme Was Doomed Before He Left Williamsburg
    Cousin Chelsea's Newport Housing Authority lease protections during Katie, Nate, Heather, and Wesley's Christmas 2004 visit to Tonomy Hill—plus the two rail and cross-border bus tariff rules Brandon Mercer never bothered to read before leaving Williamsburg.
  7. Jul 12–19, 2007 — The Unopened RRC Staff Dossier: Form A vs. Form B & The Unsigned Level 1 Contract
    Opens the internal Bates-Harding staff notes on "Prairie, Nathaniel" and "Prairie, Katie"—revealing why Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller separated their tests into Form A and Form B expecting them to cheat on the outdated 1996 exam battery, why VITA locked down the lab on Quantum OS 2000 Professional, and the drafted Level 1 Restriction & Mandatory Separation Contract sitting on their counselor's desk on Thursday morning while Katie and Nate walked off campus without passes to Heather and Wesley's Route 250 hotel.
  8. Jul 17, 2007 — The 11:00 PM Curfew Search & Why Locking the Seasonal Closet Door Got Nate and Katie Caught
    Discover how Barton Hall dorm staff tracked Nate and Katie to the Rec Hall without an on-campus sign-out sheet—and why locking a normally unlocked door in a notorious student hookup closet is the exact thing that tipped the night supervisor off while the twins were hidden in the dark.
  9. Jul 18, 2007 (1:35 AM) — Alternate 'What If' Dossier (Ending C): Angry Wesley Yanks Open the Rec Hall Door & Rescues Nate and Katie Two Hours Before Dad Arrives
    When Heather and Wesley arrive from Waynesboro in nine minutes (1:20 AM) holding Nate's 10:44 PM closet text—more than two hours ahead of David driving down from Alexandria—and RRC staff call Nate's SMS a lie, an angry Wesley drags Heather across the quad, yanks on the locked Rec Hall entrance door until the 1974 latch gives way, and marches straight to the seasonal closet to rescue Nate and Katie while furious staff demand his arrest.
  10. Jul 18, 2007 (3:50 AM) — Alternate 'What If' Dossier (Ending A): Leaving the Closet Unlocked, Heather's 10:44 PM Text, & Waking Up With Zero Clue Who's Missing
    What happens if Heather and Wesley wait out two hours of RRC's "Parent/Guardian Only" stubbornness after arriving from Waynesboro at 1:20 AM—until David Prairie finishes his two-and-a-half-hour drive down I-81 from Alexandria (3:45 AM) and flips on the closet light at 3:50 AM, waking two groggy twins who ask in complete innocence who went missing.
  11. Jul 18, 2007 (6:40 AM) — Alternate 'What If' Dossier (Ending B): Sneaking Past the Morning Janitor—And Rolling Out Into Their Own Missing-Persons Command Post
    When the panicked Night Supervisor swears on three signed state incident forms that he cleared every inch of the Rec Hall closet (claiming Nate's 10:44 PM text to Heather was a decoy), Katie and Nate sleep eight glorious hours undisturbed, pull off a silent Speed Setting 1 stealth exit past the 6:25 AM janitor, and round the boxwood hedge onto the sunlit quad—asking David, Heather, Wesley, and two police agencies who went missing.
  12. Jul 18–19, 2007 — How Christopher Vance Scrambled the Dorm Roster & The Thursday Morning Cover-Up
    What happened behind closed doors when Christopher Vance stole an open administrative login to swap opposite-gender dorm room assignments on Wednesday night (while Katie and Nate walked off campus without passes to stay in Heather and Wesley's extended-stay hotel), why RRC whisked him onto a bus in Staunton at 7:50 AM on Thursday without calling the State Police, and why RRC never said a word about Katie and Nate's missing yellow passes.
  13. Oct 28, 2010 — The 509 East 18th Street Executive Suite, Mayor Overton's Bus, & Harold Dietz's 0.4% Collapse
    Why CVTA CEO Leonard Sterling and COO Richard Halstead blackballed Nate from TRAC, the real Tidewater municipal history of the Newtown Road bus-border cliff that haunted Mayor Myra E. Overton, why Incumbent Councilman Harold Dietz left his debate podium empty on WHRC TV-15, and the internal tracking poll (44.6% to 44.2%) that triggered his fatal WTGA 790 AM radio attack on Katie's wheelchair ramp.
  14. Feb 4, 2016 — Majority Leader Callaway's Closed-Door Post-Mortem on HB 663 & The Pre-Floor Review That Never Happened
    What happened inside House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway's (R-Danville) Capitol office thirty minutes after HB 663 imploded on the floor—and the step-by-step pre-floor bill review in Room 518 with Katie and the thirteen-year-old Hawkins triplets (Sarah, Mandy, and Sam) that would have spared Delegate Martin Cobb his televised humiliation.
  15. Spring 2003 – Mar 2016 — From Smoker's Corner to Hillside Court: How Tyler Trapped Brittany on a Joint Lease & How Delegate Prairie Helped Her Exit Above Board
    How the February 2003 Varsity Soccer roast drove radioactive sleazebag Tyler out to lonely Brittany Fletcher at Smoker's Corner—talking her into dropping out at eighteen, dragging her onto a joint Hillside Court public-housing lease when her car died in 2013, her Friday midday JRTC ride without an appointment ("Hold the elevator!"), Tyler's volcanic fury seeing Heather happily married to Nate beside Katie at the church, and how Delegate Katie Prairie stayed 100% ethically above board while getting Brittany's name severed mid-lease via Va. Code § 55-248.21:2, federal VAWA lease bifurcation, and Central Virginia Legal Aid.
  16. Feb 5–6, 2016 — Why the House Page Triplets Bolted From Room 518 & How Uncle Richard Rescued Them
    Reveals how Uncle Richard Callaway and Aunt Marge rescued thirteen-year-old autistic triplets Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins in early 2015, why the triplets bolted from the doorway of Room 518 during Katie and Nate's Friday morning meltdown to fetch both Floor Leaders, and how Saturday Night Sketch (Studio 6B) wrote the viral HB 663 cold open without "cripping up."
  17. Jun 2026 – Jan 2027 — The $14 Million DSCC Primary Shock, Backing Chris Van Deren Over Schuman, The 211–204 Lame-Duck False Dawn, & The Senate Wheelchair Caucus
    Inside retiring Senator Martin Warren's office and the DSCC when Katie and Nate's bus-riding campaign defeated Preston Holloway, Uncle Richard going live on Beacon News from Danville to defend Katie against President Garrett Thorne, Katie backing Senator Chris Van Deren (D-MD) in his 29–26 caucus upset over Senator Charles Schuman (D-NY), Defense Secretary Bret Halverson's premature "total victory" lap after escaping impeachment on a 211–204 lame-duck referral vote, the Architect of the Capitol's desk upgrades for the three-member U.S. Senate Wheelchair Caucus (Senator Tess Dunmore [D-IL], Senator Katie Prairie [D-VA], and Senator Josh Novak [D-IA]), and Vice President Conrad Drayton's fury in S-216 over swearing Katie in on the U.S. Constitution.
  18. Feb 16, 2027 — Inside Dirksen Room 511: Commissioner Sterling & Director Cross's Panic
    Follow the nine stages of bureaucratic collapse inside Dirksen Room 511 as DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and RRC Director Evelyn Cross wonder how a United States Senator knows the exact color of 2007 Level 2 Barton Hall passes, the MedStrip wound-closure strips on a girl's broken nose, and the lumpy bags of curtains inside a Rec Hall storage closet—until the July 2007 math clicks (age 22) and Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence reads them the Riot Act from Richmond.
  19. Jul 22, 2027 (9:03–10:25 AM) — Governor Langford's Capitol Square Reckoning With Commissioner Sterling & Secretary Alcott
    What happened inside the Patrick Henry Building on Capitol Square twenty minutes after Katie called Governor Rebecca Langford on speakerphone from Fishersville on the exact twentieth anniversary of leaving Barton Hall—as a volcanically irate Governor confronts DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and Secretary of Health and Human Resources Dr. Miriam Alcott with Sterling's June 14 "wait out the July markup" email, lays two manila folders (5:00 PM Resignation vs. Va. Code § 2.2-106 Removal for Cause) on her mahogany table, keeps Secretary Alcott on an ice-cold final warning, and elevates Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton.
  20. Jul 22, 2027 (12:38–8:15 PM) — Arthur Lawrence's Fishersville Sweep, VITA's 120-Day Unsigned Form, & The 5:00 PM Resignations
    Follow Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence, State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton, VITA CIO Rajiv Patel, and Acting Commissioner Angela Thornton up I-64 into Fishersville at 12:38 PM—uncovering VITA's approved March 24 classroom VLAN form that Dr. Cross left unsigned for 120 days, unlocking all twelve lab workstations live by 4:15 PM, pulling lobby security video of Assistant Director Greg Saunders grabbing twenty-year-old Marcus's wheelchair push-handles alongside a June purchase order for 5,000 yellow passes, and securing Cross's and Saunders's resignations before 5:00 PM in lieu of Group III termination.
  21. Mar 2029 — Architectural & Family Guide: Two Mirrored Ground-Floor Companion Suites & Our Six-Person Alaskan King
    How David, Katie, Nate, Heather, and Brittany unveil two inch-for-inch mirrored zero-step ground-floor companion & turtle suites (Virginia Beach and Sunset Drive in Alexandria) once Senator Katie Prairie's 2028 Supported Companions, Waiver Portability, and Social Security Solvency Act takes effect—giving Wesley and Chelsea their own connected daytime sanctuary while all six continue sleeping side by side every single night on their solid-oak Alaskan King platform beds.
  22. Mar 2027 – Spring 2044 — Brenda Walsh's Suite 756 Cease-and-Desist, Thorne's Gag Order, & The 2044 Route 15 Bus-Stop Primary
    The complete story behind Brenda Walsh's unauthorized Tidewater Thorne & RTR Superstore in Suite 756 at Timberline Shopping Center (shut down by a Cease-and-Desist letter from Thorne Enterprises ten days after her own daughter voted to convict and bar Garrett Thorne for life), how a federal bail gag order (18 U.S.C. § 3142) silenced Thorne, and why fifty-eight-year-old three-term Senator Katie Prairie refused the 2044 Presidential Nomination surrounded by Nate, Heather, Wesley, Brittany, and Chelsea and forced every White House contender to interview on a live Virginia Beach transit loop ("Wait—a bus? Huh?!").

2. Alternate "What If?" Archive: Early Blueprints & Companion North Lion (books/heather) Timeline

  1. Archival Design Blueprint — Early Virginia Domicile & Ten-Campus Tour Sketch (Now Mainline Canon!)
    The original architectural design dossier that evolved directly into the mainline canon of Katie & Nathaniel—charting Aunt Linda keeping Virginia domicile for Wesley's services and Heather's in-state VDU tuition, the Summer 2003 ten-campus college tour (including RRC Redmond Hall's Safe-Person refusal), and Heather's Special Education career ladder to Prairie Twin Interactive.
  2. Alternate 'What If' Companion (books/heather) — What If Heather's Entire Family Retired to Minnesota in 2003? Maplewood Living Room (Feb 2016)
    Paired with the standalone companion novel North Lion (books/heather): explores an alternate timeline where Heather's entire family relocated to Maplewood, Minnesota in 2003 (while always keeping Wesley's bond with Nate cherished), and twenty-eight-year-old Wesley spots Katie and Nate on Meet the Nation.
  3. Alternate 'What If' Companion (books/heather) — Architectural Blueprint & Visitor Guide: Inside North Lion Scales & Tails (Maplewood, MN)
    Complete illustrated cutaway floor plan of the barrier-free Route 64 reptile conservatory featured in the standalone companion novel North Lion (books/heather).
  4. Alternate 'What If' Companion (books/heather) — Staff Member Wesley, Cousin Chelsea, & Matching Blue Gloves at the Turtle Lagoon (Jun 2018)
    In the North Lion alternate Minnesota timeline, follows Staff Member Wesley and Cousin Chelsea feeding Clover, Scooter, and Barnaby at the Maplewood conservatory lagoon.
  5. Alternate 'What If' Dossier — What If Katie and Nate Had Moved to the North Star State in 2003?
    Traces why moving Katie and Nate out of Virginia to Minnesota in 2003 would have erased Katie's Virginia transit and U.S. Senate career and left Cousins Brittany and Chelsea unrescued.
